line: Crowley on Atu II: the letter Gimel, the Moon, the path of Gimel, and Isis the Eternal Virgin (pdf p27, p61, p62, p211).

sections.title: Letter and planet
sections.line: Crowley refers the card to the letter Gimel and to the Moon (pdf p61).

quotes.quote: This card is referred to the letter Gimel, which means a Camel.

The card refers to the Moon. The Moon (being the general feminine symbol, the symbol of the second order corresponding to the Sun as the Yoni does to the Lingam) is universal, and goes from the highest to the lowest.

sections.title: The path of Gimel
sections.line: Crowley on the path of Gimel (pdf p61, p211) and on the card joining the number 1 to the number 6 (pdf p27).

quotes.quote: her path, as shown in the diagram, makes a direct connection between the Father in his highest aspect, and the Son in his most perfect manifestation.
upon him, though the Path of Gimel, the High Priestess, the triune light of Initiation.
This path is in exact balance in the middle pillar.
Consider again the card joining the number I to the number 6.

sections.title: Isis and the path upwards
sections.line: Crowley on the card as Isis the Eternal Virgin and the Artemis of the Greeks (pdf p61) and on the path which leads upwards (pdf p62).

quotes.quote: The card represents the most spiritual form of Isis the Eternal Virgin; the Artemis of the Greeks.
this is the path which leads upwards;
